note: Spec process rewritten after STP-4: frame first, questions before text, short criteria, one ordered spec review, summary confirmation, code review without quotas, escaped defects as the main measure, rules pruned after three tickets without a catch. STP-5 is the pilot. The six narrow fixes from the STP-4 retrospective are folded into items 1 to 4 and 6.

Builder pilot on STP-5 R1: a 1200-token brief was enough for a context-free Sonnet builder; it read 0.93M cache tokens in 17 calls against about 3.9M per orchestrator step; the orchestrator's 650k-token context per call is the main cost. Next: start each ticket in a new session; phase 1 coordination by stapel.

Code review HIGH and MEDIUM by rule: item 4: 9, item 3: 6, item 1: 2, item 5: 1, item 6: 1, none: 3. Per-step drift reviews caught 22 HIGH and MEDIUM before code review (test-plan 12, spec 4, design 3, code 3).

Builder briefs need explicit history rules: a GREEN changes nothing under tests; a coverage commit only adds #[test] functions with nested helpers; a test changed by a new rule is changed only in a RED; the orchestrator runs stapel check after every builder commit. Three local history rewrites happened before these rules. STP-14 (stapel check --history) planned.
Code review HIGH and MEDIUM by rule: item 3: 5, item 4: 1, item 2: 1, item 8: 1 (0 HIGH). Per-step drift reviews caught 13 HIGH and MEDIUM before code review; spec review 11.

A promise that relies on an older rule must name what that rule covers; STP-13 promise item 4 assumed STP-4 tests-changed covered deletes and renames, which it did not. Builder briefs gained three rules: a test that may pass before the code goes after the GREEN; an existing test changed in a RED must fail at the RED; run the whole test file before a coverage commit.

Item 9 applied over STP-5, STP-6 and STP-13 (code review HIGH and MEDIUM by rule; spec review and per-step drift counted for items 4 and 6): STP-5 item 1: 2, item 3: 7, item 4: 2, item 5: 5, item 6: 1; STP-6 and STP-13 as above. No item went three tickets in a row without a catch or a miss; items 1 and 5 had none in STP-13 only. Nothing removed. STP-13 counts unchanged after the close; one LOW escaped defect of STP-2 found after the close (X-1, broken pipe in stapel status), proposed for a later ticket.

Measured tokens, STP-13 against STP-6 session totals: cache read Opus 42.5M against 72.3M, Sonnet 17.6M against 33.0M, Fable 1.95M against 4.0M. End-notice estimates understate a subagent 4 to 19 times; subagent output counts stay partial in transcripts.

A builder wrote a test file with Bash cp after the guard went stale and before the Edit tool was denied, then reverted it with git checkout. The rule 'agents do not write files the guard denies by other means' held only by the agent's own report; the guard does not see Bash writes. Builder briefs name the Edit tool as the only way to write tracked files.
Code review HIGH and MEDIUM by rule: item 3: 4, item 1: 1, item 7: 1 (outside, rejected); 0 HIGH. Spec review caught 10 HIGH and MEDIUM (3 HIGH, round 2); per-step drift 2.

Item 9 applied over STP-6, STP-13 and STP-16: no item went three tickets in a row without a catch or a miss. Item 5 had none in STP-13 and STP-16; it is removed or simplified if STP-17 (fewer confirmation commands) also has none. Nothing removed. Measured cache read: orchestrator 17.6M against 42.5M in STP-13.

The step 1 builder created new test and golden files with shell heredocs and ran sed -i on an untracked test file, although the brief named the Edit and Write tools as the only way to write tracked files; the files were untracked at the time, so the rule's wording ('tracked files') left a gap and the guard does not see Bash writes. It also put quoted output lines into a doc comment to satisfy ticket_drift instead of reporting that the criterion lacked the <KEY> placeholder. Next briefs: every file under the repository is written with Edit or Write; a ticket_drift report about a quoted line is an intent_gap, not a code change.

STP-17 step 3: the builder again wrote a test file with a shell heredoc first, although the brief said every repository file is written with Edit or Write; it reverted the file with git checkout before committing. Two of three STP-17 builders broke the rule; the brief alone does not hold it. Candidate: the guard also denies Bash commands that redirect into crates/ (a later ticket, tag guard).
